Where the columns at their content widths do not fit the box (a list beside the record panel at the normal density), the data columns nobody sized give back room down to their least width (the heading on one line, never below the column floor or min_width), and a value wider than its column ends in an ellipsis on its one line (host attribute data-sf-columns-fitted); the box scrolls only when the least widths do not fit. The filter window's words follow view-config/1: tab «Представления», «Сохранить представление», «Представление сохранено».

Nothing to change. An open saved filter that holds conditions now tints the filter control as a field condition does: the phone filter icon (which had no sign of it) and the desktop «Фильтр» button with its save segment; on the phone the icon's accessible name carries the filter's name («Фильтр: Требуют внимания»).

Nothing to change. Column widths the host declares shrink toward their content before the table scrolls sideways: a list beside a docked record panel no longer scrolls while its content fits. Widths follow the text measure (C396): a column grows to at most 44 steps (352 px at normal density, was 320), the search field and toolbar end start from 44 (352, was 320), the context menu's fallback width is 44 (352, was 320), and the resource list's title measure is 52 (416, unchanged at normal density).

The View tab shows the density in effect: compact on a compact page; choosing another draws the table in it. The filter button carries the name of the open saved filter (C388, C301 (3)).

Nothing to change. A table inside a shadow root (sf-view's own) opens its row menu through SIMAI Framework sf-menu-context 1.27.0 like one in the document: the menu's for is the table's own <table> and list as elements, and the table's own right button and menu key workaround (bindShadowRowMenu) is gone. Needs the pair with sf-menu-context 1.27.0 (ui-1ed6b6c9a040 or later).

Nothing to change. New: row-offset (with total, aria-rowindex of a later page); the open record (aria-current) has the primary 12 % fill in the grid as in the list; Alt+Down / Alt+Up are left to a data view.

A host that wants the new contract passes total (the count under the filter), sort="key:dir", totals {page, all} for the columns marked total, listens to sf-view-table-open, and moves the toolbar, paging and group actions of a table standing alone to sf-view, sf-pagination and sf-bulk-actions (C295, C296). filter-text.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

clear-text.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

search-placeholder.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

create-text.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

pagination-total.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

pagination-page-size.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

page-sizes.summary: A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

context-menu-columns.summary: How many columns the settings menu splits its items into. One until a host asks for more: the read was bare for the whole life of this input, so neither its declared default nor a value a host passed ever reached the menu.

remember-widths.summary: Remember the column widths as a view preference (SF.Preferences, under preferences-key or table-settings-key) for a table no host keeps settings for; a double click on a column's edge forgets that column's width.

table-settings-key.summary: Which stored settings this table uses. Empty means the element's own id, and then its instance id, so each table on a page keeps its own. A real default here would make every table share one key and overwrite the others.

toolbar.summary: Show the built-in toolbar; a composite can provide its own toolbar slot. A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

stripes.summary: Alternate rows (zebra), the report author's choice for a wide table that is only read (owner decision C146 (4)). A person's view no longer offers it; lines between the rows and the hovered and selected row's fill are the table's own.

pin-column-label.summary: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that pins a column.

unpin-column-label.summary: Accessible name and tooltip of the control that unpins a column.

column-move-label.summary: Accessible name of the handle that moves a column in the settings list; the column label is appended to it.

column-search-placeholder.summary: Placeholder and accessible name of the search field above the column settings list.

column-search-empty-text.summary: Shown in place of the column settings list when the search matches no field.

vertical-scroll.summary: Whether the table scrolls within itself or lets the page scroll. Declared as a string with two values; the manifest previously said boolean true, which was wrong in both the type and the default.

filter-apply-text.summary: Label of the filter window’s commit button; the number of conditions a press would change is appended to it while a draft is pending. A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

layout.summary: How the records are drawn: a table, a compact list of records, or auto (the default since 1.19.0, owner decisions C31 and C146) -- a table while the table's container is at least list-below pixels wide, the list below that. `table` keeps a table at every width; in a narrow box it scrolls sideways with its first column standing still (C146 (9)). With layout-switch, the person's choice comes first.

layout-switch.summary: A list/table switch (sf-segmented, two icons) in the toolbar before Create (owner decision C31). The choice is the person's: kept with the table's preferences (preferences-key, table-settings-key or remember-widths, else for the page) and in the settings of a saved view; with it, layout table reads as auto. Below list-below there is only the list and no switch. A dated former setting of the table (C296, C295): the container's job -- sf-view, sf-pagination, sf-bulk-actions. It keeps working as before until 2027-01-01; on a table standing alone it is noted in SF.deprecations once.

list-below.summary: The container width, in pixels, below which layout auto draws the compact list.

list-fields.summary: How many fields a record shows under its title in the compact list, chosen by the columns' priority.

quick-actions.summary: The row actions a list row shows as icon buttons, always visible: their ids, comma-separated, at most three (owner decision C31). The rest stay in the row menu, which in the list is «more» (more_horiz) instead of the menu icon; on a narrow list (below 37.5rem) the quick ones fold into it too. An action without an icon is a text button.

row-open.summary: What a press on a row opens: title, the title link alone (and a double click, Enter); row, a press anywhere in the row but its controls opens the record through the same view intent (sf-view-table-apply view), in the table and in the list (owner decision C31).

size.summary: The step of the size ladder the table's controls and rows take: 1, or the dense 1/2 -- 32px controls, 14/20 text, rows of the step's height. A size of 1 written on an element the table draws becomes the table's.

preferences-key.summary: The key this table's arrangement -- order, visibility, pinning, widths -- is kept under as a view preference (SF.Preferences, sf-table/<key>); a data view passes its own. Without it table-settings-key is used, and without either nothing is kept.

row-actions-visible.summary: Where a row's action buttons are drawn: in the row under the pointer, with the focus or current (hover, the default), or in every row (always).

drag-rows.summary: Rows may be dragged out of the list as records (application/x-sf-records+json): the row's record, or every selected record when it is one of them.

row-reorder.summary: Rows can be put in another order by dragging them inside the list; a drop emits sf-table-rows-reorder {ids, before, order}. A data view sets it when the host offers row-reorder.

inline-edit.summary: The author lets the person edit at the cell. A boolean the record names in `editable` is a checkbox; a short field -- a choice, a person given options, a date, a number or money -- opens at the cell on a double press or F2: a menu of the choices, or a small popover with the field of its type and Save / Cancel (C296). Either emits sf-view-table-cell-set {id, key, value, revision}, and the cell waits for the host. Longer fields are the record card's. A data view sets it when the host offers inline-edit.

total.summary: How many records are under the filter, as the host knows it (C296, VT-4): the grid's aria-rowcount says total + 1 (the head), and a group actions bar offers «all N». 0 or absent: the rows drawn are all there is.

row-offset.summary: How many records of the filter come before the first row drawn (page 2 and on of a data view, VR2-8): with total, each row's aria-rowindex is its place in the list. 0: the rows drawn start the list. sf-view writes it with total.

bulk-actions.summary: The group actions of a table standing alone ({id, name}). Where the page's pair carries sf-bulk-actions, the table places that bar after its rows with the count, clear and «all N» (C295, C296); without it, the former outline buttons above the rows. Inside sf-view the view draws the bar. setBulkActions is a former name of the bar's actions until 2027-01-01.

columns.x-shape: columns[].key and columns[].label are the package's (ui-pro 9cbe061 table/smart.manifest.json item_contract.package_owned); width, order, visibility and pinning are a person's column settings; constant columns in a manifest give only the key, the label lives in lang roles.<role>.columns.<key> (standard 1.3.8 §11.3); columns[].list is the column's place in a list row (owner decision C31): status (a leading .sf-dot from ok, warning, error or stopped, or an option's status; the word is its tooltip and accessible text), title, supporting (joined with « · » into the second line), fact (an sf-badge without its label, in a column of one width, quiet when fine, warning or error when not) or hidden; a column with a role makes the list a list of resources, and a column without one is left to the record panel there; columns[].key_cell (true) marks a key column and columns[].key_line names the column whose value is the key cell's second line: below 44rem a table with row actions keeps the select box, the row menu and its key columns alone, without sideways scroll (owner decision C259); columns[].total (true) marks a column the totals row fills from the host's totals; columns[].options make a choice or person cell editable at the cell (inline-edit)

rows.x-shape: one entry per row: its id, its revision, and one field per column key; the vocabulary's items (§2.1), written by the host or the data view

sort.x-shape: vocabulary 1.1.5 §2.1 sort: [{key, direction}], the host's echo; a person's click is the event sort-change; also written as an attribute in its short form sort="key:asc|desc" (C296), or as JSON

totals.x-shape: {page?: {<column key>: value}, all?: {<column key>: value}}: the host's sums for the columns marked total: true, drawn as a totals row at the foot -- «На странице» and «Всего по фильтру» -- through the column's own cell format (C296). The table sums nothing itself.
totals.summary: The totals row at the foot, from the host.

current.x-shape: the id of the row the page has open; the row carries aria-current
current.summary: The id of the row the page has open: that row carries aria-current and data-current. Writing it marks the row; it does not focus it and sends no event (component.json settings.current).

selection.summary: the marked rows' ids, in row order

select.summary: The marked rows changed, vocabulary §5 select {ids}: once per change of the explicit selection, clearing included. The old name sf-port-output follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

apply.summary: A row's or the selection's action, vocabulary §5 apply: {action, scope: entry | selection, ids, revisions}. The host decides; emission is not success. The old name sf-table-action-intent follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

column-settings.summary: The column settings now in force (order, widths, pinned, hidden).

save.summary: The person's column settings, vocabulary §5 save {kind: columns, reason, columnSettings, tableSettingsKey}. The old name sf-table-column-settings-change follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

target.summary: The layer to reset. The table only resets the person's own layer.

table-settings-key.summary: The table's settings key, or null when it has none.

column-settings-reset.summary: The person asked for the default columns back. The table drops its own stored arrangement and names no defaults: the host (or a data view) resets the person's layer and answers with its defaults.

create.summary: The create button or one of its kinds, vocabulary §5 create {item}. The old name sf-table-create-intent follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

template-key.summary: The selected template's key, or an empty string.

template-label.summary: The selected template's label, or an empty string.

values.summary: The filter values now in force, keyed by filter field.

tags.summary: The active filter chips, keyed by filter field.

filter-change.summary: Request a host-side query after the active filter changes: Apply in the filter window, a chip removed, or the filter cleared. A data view turns it into query.change with filters from values. The detail is the table's getFilterPayload(): the selected template's own data fields spread first, then these four.

query.summary: A context query of the composition input port, vocabulary §5.1 query {reason, context, sequence}. The old name sf-table-query-intent follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

refresh.summary: The retry button of a failed list, vocabulary §5 refresh. The old name sf-table-retry follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

search-change.summary: Request a host-side query after the debounced search value changes.

sort-change.summary: The user activated a sortable header. Direction cycles asc, desc, null (unsorted). Intent only: the table marks the header but does not reorder rows; the host reorders or reloads.

template-delete.summary: The user deleted saved templates on the Templates tab and pressed Apply. Intent only: the host removes the saved view. One event per deleted template.

templates.summary: The saved templates: one when a template is saved from the form, several when Apply on the Templates tab changed several (order, pin, default, selected).

key.description: The template's key; a new template gets filter_template_<n>.

label.description: The name the person gave it.

selected.description: Whether it is the applied template.

data.description: The filter draft it keeps: the form values, `values` and `tags`.

filter_fields.description: The filter fields it was showing, so opening it shows them again.

settings.description: Passed through by the port as it is.

template-save.summary: Request persistence of one or more filter templates (order, pin, delete, default, selected flags or data): detail {templates}, one entry or several. Loading a saved view is reported by sf-table-template-select.

template-select.summary: The user applied a different saved template on the Templates tab. Intent only: the host loads that saved view.

toolbar-action.summary: The user chose one of the view's own actions from the toolbar menu. Intent only, and cancelable: the component follows an item's same-site href unless the host takes the navigation over with preventDefault.

expand.summary: A tree row opened or closed, vocabulary §5 expand {id, expanded}. The old name sf-table-tree-toggle follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

load-more.summary: The next page of a tree level, vocabulary §5 load-more {direction: after, parent, cursor}. The old name sf-table-tree-more follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

ids.summary: The ids dragged: every selected id when the dragged row is selected, otherwise that row's id alone.

source.summary: Where the rows come from: the table's preferences-key, table-settings-key or id, or null.

rows-drag.summary: Rows began to be dragged out of a list with drag-rows, for a drop target such as a tree; the same {ids, source} rides in the drag data as application/x-sf-records+json.

move.summary: Rows put in another order, vocabulary §5 move {ids, before, order}. The old name sf-table-rows-reorder follows once with its old detail until 2027-01-01 (aliases.json).

cell-set.summary: A cell was edited at its place: a checkbox pressed, or a short field chosen in its menu or saved in its popover (C296): the record, the field, the new value and the record's revision.

window.summary: The rows drawn of a long list changed (standard 1.3.8 §18.4): {first, last}, row indexes in the list.

layout-change.summary: The person chose the list or the table with the layout switch (or set-layout was called); the choice is already kept. sf-view keeps it with the view.

open.summary: The person opened a record: its title pressed, the row double pressed or Enter (newTab false), or the title with a modifier or the middle button where the record has an address (newTab true). Said beside the view intent; the host opens the record card or follows the address (C296).

add-rows.summary: Append another backend page for show-more mode.

apply-query-result.summary: Apply rows answering the newest pending context query. Returns false and changes nothing for a stale, repeated or unknown sequence.

clear-selection.summary: Clear the explicit selection of this instance; emits the selection port once when it changes.

request-action-intent.summary: Emit a typed row or bulk action request; the host owns execution and authorization. Invalid arguments throw TypeError before emission.

request-create-intent.summary: Emit sf-table-create-intent for the main button (null) or a declared create item id.

request-retry.summary: Emit a retry intent after a failed data request.

set-sort.summary: Show the host's current sort on the headers without emitting an event; (null, null) clears it.

toggle-tree-row.summary: Say that a tree row was opened or closed (sf-table-tree-toggle).

request-tree-more.summary: Ask for the next page of a tree level (sf-table-tree-more).

focus-row.summary: Bring a row into view and give it the focus (the grid's one Tab stop).

set-layout.summary: Choose the list or the table for this person, as the layout switch does: kept with the table's preferences and drawn. Refused for another value; unchanged when it is the choice already.

scroll-to-row.summary: Bring a row into view inside the table's own scroll, drawing it first when the window has not (C296); the focus stays where it was. Answers applied, or rejected for an unknown id.

empty.summary: Shown in place of the built-in empty state when there are no rows (C296).

error.summary: Shown in place of the built-in error state; absent, the empty slot or the built-in error (C296).

relations.name: cl-reference-link
$comment: The cells drawn with another Smart element come with the table, not
after the rows: a reference (sf-reference-link), a file
(sf-file-preview) and a colour (sf-input-color, in a cell as well as in a
card). Fetched lazily, each upgraded some 600 ms after the rows had
drawn and moved the row (stand 24: CLS 0.0145 at 1280 when the data
arrived).

relations.name: cl-input-country
$comment: A string whose variant is a phone draws sf-input-country. The rule fence
reads a component's own templates, and this element comes from the shared
renderer set instead -- so nothing would have caught its absence until a
page showed an element that never upgraded.

relations.name: cl-empty-state
$comment: A table without rows says why in sf-empty-state (owner, 2026-10-14).

relations.name: cl-tabs
$comment: The filter window's tabs, «Шаблоны» and «Поля» (owner, 2026-10-14).

relations.name: cl-settings
$comment: The gear's window is sf-settings in its panel look, «Поля» and «Вид» (owner decision C106).

relations.name: cl-sortable
$comment: The windows' lists are reordered with sf-sortable (owner, 2026-10-13).

relations.name: cl-radio
$comment: The filter window's templates are a radio list: a page with nothing else
using sf-radio drew its rows empty (owner, 2026-10-14).

relations.name: cl-resizer
$comment: A column's edge is the Framework's resize gesture (owner, 2026-10-14).

relations.name: dot
$comment: The list of resources (C31): the status dot is the dot component's class markup.

relations.name: tooltip
$comment: The status word, a fact's note and a quick action's name are the Framework tooltip (its anchor and data-tooltip), shown on hover and on keyboard focus: behaviour, fetched after the page is ready.

relations.name: cl-segmented
$comment: The layout switch in the toolbar (C31).

relations.name: align-items/default
$comment: The utility classes its templates write, asked for with the component (SIMAI Framework loader: a Framework component gets them from template-utilities.generated.json, a package component names them here); fetched after the first paint, they moved the drawn parts -- the bulk band's gap came 0 -> 8 and the band 8 px down some 150 ms in (View 1.8.1 acceptance, queue #172). The list is scripts/generate-template-utilities.mjs run over the overlay.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

skeleton.$comment: The rows arrive after the first paint (the data view, or the host, sets them): the derived skeleton (static/default/<example>.skeleton.html) holds their box until they do, and the element keeps it until rows are set (standard 1.3.8 §5.4). Derived rather than skeleton.html: a row is a cell per column, and the template syntax repeats one level (first-paint-skeleton.mjs).

--sf-view-table-row-block-size.x-summary: read by a page: the row's box at the table's size (size 1 or 1/2), so a page keeps the place before the first paint; set by the sheet (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-head-block-size.x-summary: read by a page: the head row's box at the table's size; set by the sheet (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-edge.x-summary: the author's: the inline inset of the first and last cell (default --sf-space-1) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-line-color.x-summary: the author's: the colour of the lines between rows and under the head (default the table's outline) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-head-color.x-summary: the author's: the head's ink (default --sf-on-surface-variant) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-row-background-color.x-summary: the author's: a row's own fill, a zebra with data-sf-view-stripes (default the page surface) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-selected-background-colo.x-summary: the author's: a selected row's fill (default --sf-primary-container) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-view-table-title-lines.x-summary: the author's: how many lines a title cell takes before it is cut (default 2) (C296; public, eight --sf-view-table-*)

--sf-table-row-block-size-1/2.x-summary: published on :root, set by the sheet, read by a page: a one-line row at the step, size 1/2 (docs.md, the list's box); a former public name until 2027-01-01 beside the eight --sf-view-table-* (C296)

--sf-table-row-block-size-1.x-summary: published on :root, set by the sheet, read by a page: a one-line row at the step, size 1 (docs.md, the list's box); a former public name until 2027-01-01 beside the eight --sf-view-table-* (C296)

Context menus are anchored to their opener with SF.Position: they flip and shift at the viewport edge and follow the opener on scroll; the filter chip menu opens under the chip instead of the viewport corner.

Filter chips are keyboard operable: each chip label is a button (sf-tag interactive) beside its remove action; Enter or Space opens the chip menu, anchored to the chip, and Escape returns focus to the chip.
The built-in record modal ignores modal:after-close events of nested modals now that modal events bubble.
The manifest moves to smart-component-manifest v2: persistence, ownership, security, accessibility and state use the v2 shape, and adapter, artifacts and readiness are declared.

Declare the data view as a composition type (smart.view-table): the projection now carries the intents it raises, the data it accepts and where its settings key lives, instead of dropping them.

The empty brick takes heading and the filter's avatars heading, the names sf-empty-state and sf-avatar read since 1.3.8. No public attribute, property or event of sf-view-table changes.

From component.json (standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8): events by the vocabulary's verbs -- sf-table-apply, -select, -save, -create, -query, -refresh, -expand, -load-more, -move -- with the old names as dated aliases until 2026-12-01 (aliases.json); onSearchEnd, onTemplateSave, onFilterUpdate, onColumnSettingsChange and sf-table:column-settings-change follow once each, noted in SF.deprecations.

Many entries (§18.4, simai/ui-pro#2): from 300 rows only the rows in view and a margin are drawn, reported as sf-table-window {first, last}; a plain cell is class markup; one changed row is redrawn in place.
The data state ready, populated its alias; current marks the open row (aria-current); actions answer outcomes.

The windows' portal is watched by the Loader (SF.Loader.watch) and lazy elements are asked for through SF.Loader.ensure; needs core.runtime >= 1.19.0. Nothing to change for a host on a pair from core.runtime 1.19.0 on.

Draws and finds the renamed Framework elements by their new tags (the row and column menus are sf-menu-context (its sf-menu-context-* events), the icon buttons sf-button-icon, the typed cells and editors sf-input-color, sf-input-country, sf-input-date and sf-slider-range; a component type that names a former tag (a host's {type: 'icon-button'}) draws the element under its current tag (canonicalTag of the Smart base)); the rule relations name cl-<new>. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with the tag renames (core.runtime 1.21.0). No visible change. Nothing to change for a host on that pair; a host that writes the former tags keeps working until 2027-01-01.

The tag is sf-view-table (rename plan R2, naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>); the folder view-table, the id smart.view-table and the bundle cl-view-table follow it (were table, smart.data-view, cl-table). sf-table stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: old markup upgrades as this element, the Loader forwards cl-table, and every event fires under its former name as well, with the same detail. Public CSS variables and classes keep their names. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair whose package reference lists the former tag (core.runtime 1.22.0). Nothing to change for a host until 2027-01-01; new markup writes sf-view-table.

A date, date and time or time the host does not format reads in the page's language («2 нояб. 2026 г.», «15 нояб. 2026 г., 10:30», «09:30») instead of as stored; a host's formatFieldValue still wins. An html cell shows its text, not its markup; a cell of several files shows each file's name with its icon. The settings column is left out when it would open nothing (no settings-menu, no row actions, no row-reorder). Nothing to change for a host; a host that relied on stored dates in cells formats them in formatFieldValue.

A filter option drawn as a badge is a tight badge (sf-badge tight, SIMAI Framework sf-badge 1.3.0): it keeps the size's own narrow side room in the dense option list, as a table cell's choice badge does. Needs the pair with sf-badge 1.3.0 (ui-2a671352d67b or newer) to show; on an older pair the attribute is ignored and the badge is as before. Nothing to change for a host.

Its windows -- the filter, field and settings windows and the menus -- are a surface of the document's one layer stack (standard 1.3.8 §19): a press outside closes them through the stack's one listener and Escape through the stack, only while they are the top layer, and they are drawn at the stack's z-index (--sf-z-index-layer and its step) where they read --sf-z-index-9 before; --sf-table-context-menu--z-index still wins. The table bound a document click and keydown of its own: Escape on a window inside a record panel closed the panel too, and a press outside a drawer closed the drawer together with the window over it; now the window closes first. A press on the control that opened a window is still that control's (the gear opens and closes its window). Nothing to change for a host.

sf-view-table-template-save carries {templates}: a list of one template (saved from the form) or several (Apply on the Templates tab), each {key, label, selected, data, settings}, at least one (the decision 'Event detail that is not a flat object', 2026-11-09). The detail used to be the template object itself or an array of them. sf-table-template-save and onTemplateSave keep that former detail through the element's adapter (mode split) until their dates. A host listening to sf-view-table-template-save reads detail.templates; sf-view 1.10.0 does, and still reads a bare template or array until 2027-01-01.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-cb287da78ab1 (core.runtime 1.45.0; the set needs 1.43.0 or newer): the theme roles by their C16 names (--sf-surface-page, --sf-surface-popup, --sf-shadow-popup, --sf-on-surface-popup-variant, --sf-primary-outline, --sf-primary-state-select; the former names are dated aliases of the same values), the icon buttons and buttons ask for appearance ghost (link is its former name, drawn the same). The reference names one args argument per action (standard §4.4); every method the class writes already read the object form beside the fields in order (isActionParameters), and addRows, requestCreateIntent and focusRow also a bare value (x-registry.action-calls). Nothing changes on the page.

The avatar's max-width reads --sf-table-avatar--max-width with the fallback none: a host may still bound the avatar, and a page that sets nothing draws what it drew (the bare reference was unset, so none). The pair range no longer lists a variable bound by the page. Nothing changes on the page.

The list of resources (owner decision C31, 2026-11-09): columns[].list names a column's place in a list row -- status, title, supporting, fact or hidden. With one, a list row is the status dot (its word the tooltip and the accessible text; a stopped resource's word also leads the second line), the title over the supporting fields joined with « · », the facts as sf-badge without labels in columns of one width (8rem; quiet when fine, warning or error when not, the column's label read to a screen reader), then the quick actions and «more». The row is a row of the ladder: 48 at size 1/2, 56 at size 1, 52 on a phone with the title a text step larger. Below 37.5rem only the most worrying fact stays and the quick actions fold into «more». A list without roles is drawn as before.

quick-actions (ids, at most three) draws those row actions as icon buttons in every list row, always visible, with the Framework tooltip; the rest are the «more» menu (more_horiz), which replaces the row menu icon in the list; a narrow list folds the quick ones into it. row-open="row" (the default is title): a press anywhere in a row but its controls opens the record (the view intent, as the title link); the title link is the list row's tab stop, and the arrows, Home and End move from it as from the row (they did nothing in the list before: the focus went only to table rows).

layout-switch: an sf-segmented list/table in the toolbar before Create; the person's choice is kept with the table's preferences (the preference record's layout field) and in a saved view's settings (settings.layout), sent by layout-change and the action set-layout. A list chosen on a wide container keeps the table's toolbar with the switch; below list-below the compact list and its toolbar, no switch.

One row model on the ladder for every table (the look points the owner accepted on 2026-11-09): a body cell's block padding is the rung of two lines of the step's text less those lines and the row's line -- --sf-ui-2--control-height at size 1/2, --sf-ui-3--control-height at size 1 -- and a body row stands on the rung between (block-size --sf-ui-1--control-height at 1/2, --sf-ui-2--control-height at 1). At size 1/2 a one-line row with its box and menu is 40 (it was 45), two lines -- a link with its supporting text or a text wrapped to two lines -- 48 (they were 48 and 53), three lines 68. At size 1 a one-line row with the row menu is 48 (it was 73), two lines 56 (53 and 81 before). The head keeps the step's space around its line, at size 1 from the control ladder (--sf-ui-1--space-y) rather than --sf-space-1: 41, 57 with the box (it was 57 and 73). The published --sf-table-row-*-block-size-* say the same rows (40, 48, 48, 56; head 33, 41). Under compact page density the ladder moves one rung down and the rows with it; a person's view density (data-sf-view-density) keeps its padding.

A column with a list role draws the same value in a table cell: a status as the dot with its word, a fact as its badge (quiet, warning or error, with its tip). The row the person is on (data-current, where the keys and a press leave them) is kept apart from the record the page has open (current, aria-current): the keys no longer move the open record, and list rows carry aria-current as table rows do. Under compact density (data-sf-density="compact", C22, desktop) a table without a size takes the ladder one rung down: 40 with the row's controls, 48 with a supporting line (it was 57 and 61), and the published step-1 box follows on a compact page.

The list's look points (owner, 2026-11-09): the record's title is the surface's text colour (--sf-on-surface), medium weight, underlined while the row is pointed at or the link focused (it was the link colour), and the link draws no ring of its own inside the row's ring. The open record (current, aria-current) has the primary container fill (--sf-primary-container: 12 light, 24 dark); the row the keyboard is on shows the focus ring only. On a phone the row's buttons and «more» are --sf-ui-1--control-height (36; 28 at size 1/2 before). The list has no inline padding and an empty toolbar start takes no gap, so the search field, Create and the rows' fill are on one line (R077). The quick actions still fold below a 37.5rem container.

The controls inside are relative (C22, Larena 2026-11-10): a table without a size writes no size on its toolbar (filter, search, Create, gear, layout switch, chips), its menus or the row controls it draws; a component a column or an action names at size 1 takes the host's size, or none when the host has none. Compact page density then moves them a rung down with the page (32 at 1280); a host with size="1" or "1/2" hands that size down as before.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-a0370c0c99fb (core.runtime 1.49.0; the set still needs 1.43.0 or newer). New relations: dot, tooltip, cl-segmented. Nothing to change for a host that does not use the new settings.

The head row is on the ladder (D2 of the view 1.6.0 acceptance): it is a one-line row of its step, with the rows' padding and rung -- 40 at size 1/2 and 48 at size 1 beside rows with the box and menu, whether it holds the box and sortable column controls or only their names (it was 45 and 57 with the controls, 37/33 and 41 without). --sf-table-head-block-size-* follow: 40 and 48 (they said 33 and 41).

The published box agrees with the drawn tables under page density (C22, D3 of the 1.6.0 acceptance): a written size is stronger than density, so the -1/2 names are the size="1/2" table on every page -- 40, 48 and head 40 on a compact page too (they gave 36, 40 and 29) -- and the -1 names are the table without a size in the density of the element they are read on (40/48/40 on a compact page). The names are also declared on every element with data-sf-density, so a data-sf-density="normal" region of a compact page reads the normal box (the size="1" table there).

A draw reads the column settings once (simai/ui-pro#1): getColumnSetting() takes them from the draw while the template is built; counted over one setRows() draw, 8 rows asked getColumnSettings() 268 times and 60 rows 343, now 4. An idle row's actions cell is the bare <td> (simai/ui-pro#2): the buttons are bound on the cell, so a row of five columns with its box, menu and actions is 29 nodes (31), the buttons still come with the pointer, the focus and the current row, and the row is not drawn anew when they do. Nothing to change for a host.

On a selected list item, the open record (aria-current) and a selected table row, --sf-surface-underlay is the place's solid colour (--sf-surface-place-solid, else --sf-surface-place, so a selected row on a soft place leaves the badge alone), so a tonal badge on that translucent fill lays its tone over a solid base (C43, D1 of the 1.6.0 acceptance: a warning badge on the open record read grey). It needs the SIMAI Framework roles --sf-surface-underlay and --sf-surface-place-solid (ui-source fix/c43-badge-on-place c6711098, the next pair, core.runtime 1.50.0 or newer); on an older pair the line does nothing.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-2bd5a3ab478a (ui-source d25a01f9989d, core.runtime 1.51.0), which the set now needs (core.runtime 1.51.0 or newer): the pair that carries the roles --sf-surface-underlay and --sf-surface-place-solid. Nothing to change for a host on that pair.

The table's own windows by their kind (owner decision C32, 2026-11-09), from the Framework's popup widths, which follow density: the filter with its saved views (filter-settings) and the column settings (table-settings) are panels, --sf-popup-panel-width (20rem; 18rem compact) or the trigger's width when wider; saving a template (filter-favorites) and a chip's own filter (tag-settings) are forms, --sf-popup-form-width (20rem; 18rem compact), where they were as wide as their content (295 / 283 compact / 250 on a phone, now 320 / 288 / 320). A panel in several columns (context-menu-columns) is as wide as its columns. --sf-table-context-menu--max-width still caps every window, and the room a window has caps it. The menus (create, list sort, row and toolbar actions) are sf-menu-context's rows and keep its menu widths (10-18rem).

The content table of an sf-view whose code has not arrived yet does not draw on its own (DEV decision msg-e39bb812, zero toolbar shift when saved views are declared): the Loader defines the table before the view, and the table drew its own toolbar -- the search field across the whole row, the filter button and the saved-views control coming in a frame later -- for a frame or two before the view's first paint replaced it with the skeleton, so the toolbar moved by the controls' width (182 px with saved views declared and 142 px without at 1440; at 390 the bar went from 80 to 36 px tall). It draws once sf-view is defined, with the settings the view gave it, and the first toolbar on the page is the skeleton, which stands where the answer draws it. A table whose static markup the server printed is adopted as before. Nothing to change for a host.

Also 1.18.1 (saved-views r2, DEV acceptance D1): the first render reads the width of the table's box before it draws, so at 390 a table whose answer was in when its code was defined draws the compact toolbar and the list from its first frame; it drew the desktop toolbar first (80-124 px, then 36), because the box was measured only after the first paint.

Also 1.18.1 (D2): the content table waits for sf-view at most 3 s, or half a second after the view's script errs, then draws on its own without the view's toolbar and warns once; a view whose code never came left the area blank.

Rows name their fill to SIMAI Framework core mix sf-place-fill (C43 D3, D4): a hovered, selected, open and selected-and-hovered row, in the table and in the phone list, declares --sf-surface-underlay as the row's own opaque base (--sf-table-row--background-color, else --sf-surface-page) and --sf-surface-place-fill as the tint it paints. A tonal badge on the row lays its tone over the base, and an anchored badge's ring takes the row's tint over the place, where it cut the hovered row's tint out to the bare place colour. Selected and open rows took the place's solid colour as the underlay; they take the row's base now, which is what is under their tint. On a pair without the roles the lines do nothing.

The busy overlay's spinner carries its words as label with label-hidden (owner decision C138; SP-06 of the skeleton and spinner study) instead of an empty label and an aria-label, so the spinner keeps one name mechanism and the status region says the words once. label-hidden ships with sf-spinner 1.4.0 in the next SIMAI Framework pair; on an older pair the attribute is ignored and the words show beside the spinner, so this version is released over a pair with sf-spinner 1.4.0.

A list empty only because of its filters says so by its glyph (owner decision C120 (3)): the nothing-found brick draws filter_alt_off (sf-empty-state icon); found nothing by a search, or by a search and filters, keeps the brick's own search_off.

A row's text starts where the SIMAI Framework table now puts it: the published --sf-table--row-text-inset is the cell spacing plus --sf-space-1 (16 at 1440, 12 under compact density and on a phone), the edge inset a list row has, which the table classes give the first cell from utility.table 1.3.0 (ui-source fix/table-classes-g4, C77, C105 H6); it was the cell spacing plus --sf-a8, the 8 every cell had. sf-view-properties pulls a related list out by this number, so the list's row text stays on the field-label axis (with the old number it would stand 8, 4 compact, off it). Needs the SIMAI Framework pair with utility.table 1.3.0; over an older pair a related list stands 8 (4) left of the labels. Made in ui-pro first (fix/pro-g4 as 1.17.3, 2026-11-14) and taken here. Nothing to change for a host.

The table of owner decision C146 (prototypes/table-study.html, research TB rows). (1) A row is a control of its step: 40 at 1, 32 at 1/2 and under compact density, a row with a second line 48 (40 compact); the head row is as tall as the rows. (2) The head is quiet: medium weight, --sf-on-surface-variant, no fill of its own beyond the surface, one line under it. (3) A number column (integer, number, money, percent) is end-aligned, its digits tabular, never wrapped; its sort mark stands before the label. (4) Lines between rows, the hovered and the selected row's fill; alternate rows only when the report author writes stripes (new boolean setting, default false) -- the person's «Вид» no longer offers stripes, and a stored stripes preference is ignored.

(5) Row actions, variant В (owner remark R239): the row menu «≡» at the start of the row after the box, named «Действия: <name>», holds every action of the row; the hover-only «Действия» column is gone; the main field -- the title column, else the first data column with a plain value -- is the link that opens the record (a real href opens in a new tab or with the middle button); the right button on a row opens the same menu (Shift+right button and the right button on a link keep the browser's), and so do Shift+F10 and the menu key; on a selected row that menu acts on every selected row (headed «Выбрано N», the actions they share), a row outside the selection becomes the selection first, and «Удалить» comes last after a divider (C164). The column-settings gear stays in the «≡» column's head. Bulk action buttons are regular (outline on-surface, C116), the one that deletes the outlined danger and last; a checked row box draws its tick (the box markup had no glyph). A cell's sf-badge is tonal (C140) unless the host asks for outline. (6) The sort mark shows only on the sorted column, arrow_upward or arrow_downward. (7) A title runs to two lines and ends in an ellipsis; a clipped title carries the whole text in a SIMAI Framework tooltip. (8) A table with actions is a grid (role grid): one Tab stop, the arrows move between the controls of a row and between rows, Home/End and Ctrl+Home/End, Shift+F10 or the menu key opens the row's «≡»; the column-resize edges are no Tab stops (resizer study RS-10), a width is set by the pointer. (9) layout defaults to auto (TB-11): below list-below the records are the list; a plain table (layout table) on a narrow screen scrolls in its frame with its first column standing still -- the title column, else the first data column. The empty state stands in the visible part of the frame on a phone (TB-12). Hosts: a host that relied on the stripes preference sets the stripes attribute; a host that read the «Действия» column (key actions) reads the «≡» menu.

Every menu of the table is on the table's step (owner remark 2026-11-15, recipe-list-toolbar): the row menu (data-sf-table-menu="row"), which lives on <body> or in the open dialog, had no size and fell back to the menu's own 1/2 (32 px rows, 14 px text) beside a table of size 1 (rows 48, text 16). On every opening it now takes the table's resolved size (the size attribute, else the default 1) and the density of the table's area (data-sf-density, core followDensity); the menus the table draws itself (settings, filters, sort, create, tags, toolbar actions, template actions) take the resolved size too, where they took it only from a written attribute. Size 1 is 40 px rows and 16 px text (32 and 14 under compact density), 1/2 is 32 and 14 (28 compact). Works on the released pair ui-7fb26d395af2; SIMAI Framework fix/menu-opener-size makes every menu without a size follow its opener as well. Nothing to change for a host.

The view's actions button in the toolbar and a filter template's actions button draw ⋯ (more_horiz), not ⋮ (more_vert): owner decision C155 (2), defect TL-1 of the ui-pro admin set (K-1). A right click on a row opens the row's menu at the pointer, its corner at the point (C164 (1), ui-control research 2026-11-14-context-menu CM-1; sf-menu-context's point anchor, a fixed box of no size removed when the menu closes); it opened under the row's ≡ button. The keys still open it at that button. The list's rows (layout list, the narrow table) get the same: a right click, the context-menu key and Shift+F10 open the list their own button opens -- the ≡ of a plain list every action, the ⋯ of a list with quick actions what the row does not show (all of them while a narrow list folds the quick ones away); before, only the button opened it. A link, a field and Shift with the right button keep the browser's menu, as in the table. Nothing to change for a host.

A list row's context menu follows the table's selection rule (C164 (3), dispatcher decision: one behaviour for both layouts): a right click, the context-menu key or Shift+F10 on a selected list row opens the menu over the whole selection -- the «Выбрано N» heading and only the actions every selected row offers, a choice acting on all of them -- and on a row outside the selection that row becomes the selection first, as in the table. Before, the list opened the row's own button list and left the selection as it was. With one row (alone or the only selected) the list keeps its own button's list (C164 (2)): the ≡ of a plain list every action, the ⋯ of a list with quick actions what the row does not show. Table and list go through one path (openRowContextMenu over rowMenuTargets); a second opening while the first waits for the redraw of a new selection is ignored in both. Nothing to change for a host.

Over the SIMAI Framework pair ui-141822273efe a size 1/2 table is 32 again (28 compact, 28 on a phone): the row holds the step and its cells follow it. The Framework's class table puts the step-1 control height on every cell since utility.table 1.4.0 (C146 (1)), which held every size 1/2 row and the head at 40 (36 on a phone) and the published --sf-table-row-block-size-1/2 and --sf-table-head-block-size-1/2 no longer were the rows drawn. Size 1 is unchanged. The toolbar holds its own gaps (12 between its groups, 8 inside them, the steps its gap-1/2 and gap-1/3 classes name): the class sheet is a utility the Loader fetches when it sees the class, and a table drawn before its sheets moved its search field by 12 px (16 in the list toolbar) when it came. Nothing to change for a host.

The printed first paint and the drawn table lay the columns out by one rule (standard 1.3.8 gate 24): every data column at its content width on one line, the last data column nobody sized taking the spare room, the select, settings and actions columns at their declared widths. The unmeasured content-sized table had shared the spare room between every column and drew the select column as wide as its box's label wanted (50 against 42), and the measured widths were rounded up to the 4px grid with a pixel to spare, so every printed cell moved when the code measured (typed-cells: CLS 0.035 at 1280, 0.041 at 1440, 0.002 at 390). The measured width is now the content's own (the printed first paint carries no measured width, §5.4, and is laid out in the page's own face); the spare-room column is marked in the markup (data-sf-spare-room on its col); a table with rows is content-sized from its first render, where it was drawn for a frame as a fixed table as wide as its content; a content-sized table takes no column floor (the spare-room column stood at 160 on a phone, wider than its content). The column window's footer stands on the menu's own inset (SIMAI Framework C105 H4, C106): the table zeroed sf-menu-context's inline content padding, from which the head, the top and the footer take their margin, so the footer's buttons stood 11 from the panel's padding edge while the search and the rows stood at 15 (the plates' inset 3 plus the item inset 12, where the Framework's panel rows put their text); the window's blocks now start on one axis. Nothing to change for a host.

A table with selection boxes asks the Loader for the tick («check») and the head's «remove» with its first icon font (SF.Loader.preloadIcons, as sf-segmented and sf-input ask for the glyphs they will draw). An unchecked row's glyph is empty, so the page's font never had the tick and the first box checked waited for a second font before its tick showed (0.6 s on a fast line, longer on a slow one; DEV recipes p1, owner remark). Nothing to change for a host.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-078a4b4c6f6e (ui-source 10145e63b9dc) the Framework file it builds in, src/smart/pagination/index.js (sf-pagination 1.7: «Show more» within reach, C167; a deleting action listed last, C116), moved; the provenance and the version follow. Nothing of its own; nothing to change for a host. 1.19.7 and 1.19.8 are ui-pro's own patched copies, never this set's.

C259: below 44rem a table with row actions keeps the select box, the row menu and its key columns (columns[].key_cell) alone without sideways scroll, the key cell carries a second line (columns[].key_line); one row menu (sf-menu-context for=) over table and list rows, every action of the row in it; row menus follow the host's row actions, not row-actions
C144: the list toolbar's field, view buttons (filter and sort, 1/3 apart) and Создать are three groups --sf-space-1 apart (12 on a phone, was 8)
#172: the utility classes its templates write are its relations, asked for with the component; fetched after the first paint they moved the drawn parts (the bulk band 0 -> 8 gap, 8 px down)
PRO-ADM-9: a resource row's more button names its record (Ещё действия: <name>), as the row menu button does (Действия: <name>)

C158 (5): a column's width from the keyboard -- the table stays one Tab stop, the arrows walk the heads (a head with an edge and no sort button is a stop itself), Enter, Shift+F10, the menu key or the right button on a head with an edge opens «Изменить ширину · По содержимому · По умолчанию»; «Изменить ширину» takes the focus to the edge, whose arrows set the width through SIMAI Framework SF.Resizer.attach (sf-resizer 1.3.0), Enter or Escape go back to the head; «По содержимому» fits the column to its head and values on one line, kept as the person's width; «По умолчанию» drops it, as a double click on the edge still does. The edge's name and value («27 %») are words of the language files. Space on a sort button still sorts.

SIMAI Pro follow-ups: filter chips stand --sf-space-1/4 apart (C105 H5; were 8) and are written with their current names (kind=default, active, sf-tag-close; were type, root-class=active and the dated close); the search fields carry the glass at the start, the field's own clear and a name (icon-start, clearable, aria-label; C123, C153 (6), TI-10); a group action's button and a host action with menu row-settings open the one standard row menu (C164 (2), CM-8) -- the hand-drawn second row menu is gone.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-24d64b7f6eb7 (ui-source 40541c0c4fba, core.runtime 1.59.0) the Framework file it builds in, src/smart/pagination/index.js, moved; the provenance and the version follow. Nothing of its own; nothing to change for a host.

Former names (aliases.json, every alias that ended 2026-12-01) now end 2027-01-01 (draft set standard §13.4, view round 1 G1): no alias may end before the main consumer moves to the set, Larena on data-sf-sets="admin view" on 2026-12-15, with at least two weeks' margin. The old names keep coming as before; nothing to change for a host.

Over SIMAI Framework ui-24d64b7f6eb7: its icon buttons and buttons ask for the look ghost where they asked for link, ghost's former name (component.icon-buttons 1.14.0, sf-button-icon 1.13.3, sf-button 1.16.3, RG-IB-1..3, C213); the printed row menu wrote sf-icon-button--link, which the pair answers with a console warning. sf-port-output.summary: Composition port output. The table emits port selection (record-ids.v1) once per change of its explicit selection, including clearing; a common sf-composition-scope routes it.

sf-table-action-intent.summary: Request one host-resolved row or bulk operation. Event source is the owning table instance; emission is not operation success.

sf-table-column-settings-change.summary: Request persistence of a column preference delta after resize, reorder or visibility changes.

sf-table-create-intent.summary: The user pressed the create button (item null) or chose an item from its menu (item id). Intent only: the host opens its create form.

sf-table-query-intent.summary: Request a host-side query after the context input port changed. The host resolves the relation and access, then answers with applyQueryResult(sequence, rows); older sequences are ignored.

sf-table-retry.summary: Request another host-side load after the error state.

sf-table-tree-toggle.summary: The person opened or closed a tree row. The data view answers it; the table only says which row and whether it was open.

sf-table-tree-more.summary: The person asked for the next page of one tree level.

sf-table-rows-reorder.summary: Rows were dragged into another order inside the list: the ids that moved, the row they now stand before (null: the end) and the whole order shown.

getActiveFilterFieldKeys.summary: Which filter fields the filter is showing, in the host's field order.

getFilterPayload.summary: Read the current filter draft for host-side query validation.

getInstanceId.summary: Identity of this instance: the author's id when there is one, an own counter otherwise. Ids, the settings key fallback and the portal derive from it.

getQueryContext.summary: Read the immutable context last received through the context input port, or null.

getSelectedRecordIds.summary: Read the typed record identities selected in this table result, without DOM parsing.

getSort.summary: Read the sort shown on the headers.

getToolbarActions.summary: The toolbar actions as declared, copied.

requestContextQuery.summary: Internal to the context port: emit sf-table-query-intent for the current context with a new pending sequence.

setActiveFilterFields.summary: Show exactly these filter fields in the selected filter template. Used when a saved view is opened: settings.filter_fields names the fields it was showing.

setBulkActions.summary: Register labeled opaque actions for the current selection. Empty selection disables their controls.

setCreateItems.summary: Set the create split-button menu items ({id, name} only). Without items the create button has no arrow.

setDataState.summary: Switch between automatic, loading, populated, empty and error presentation states.

setFilterFields.summary: Register backend-allowlisted filter fields and controls.

setRows.summary: Replace the current backend result rows.

setTableData.summary: Patch columns, rows or related table state supplied by the host.

setTableSettings.summary: Apply a column-preference delta without emitting a save request.

setToolbarActions.summary: Declare the view's own actions for the toolbar menu: {id, label, icon?, href?}. An href must name this same site. Without actions the control is not rendered.

sfPortInput.summary: Composition input port entry used by sf-composition-scope. Accepts only the declared context port with record-ids.v1; invalid ports or values throw TypeError before any state change.

isTree.summary: Whether the rows are a tree: some row carries __tree, written by the data view from the host's levels.

treeColumnKey.summary: The column a tree hangs from: the title column, or the first data column.

aria-label.description: The table's accessible name. Read it from the props context and never from the element: `aria-label` is reflected by the platform, so element.ariaLabel returns null with no attribute set and shadows what the component resolves. Whether an English default belongs in a family whose other fourteen text inputs default to Russian is the owner's open question about the Framework's default language.
